patterns.context: Acts as a copula or auxiliary after the subject, especially when introducing identity, composition, state, or attributes; occurs in varied word orders.
patterns.domain: Website introductions, forums, encyclopedias, and general English text

patterns.name: Perfect have been
patterns.context: Often followed by a state or ongoing description, as in “have been working”; occurs alongside present-tense structures and subjects such as companies and institutions.
patterns.domain: Company information, academic papers, and review text

patterns.name: Other English function words and constructions
patterns.context: In fluent English sentences, these words occur near subject-predicate structures, linking, or time expressions, but no consistent independent trigger is apparent.
patterns.domain: Websites, email, academic papers, sports reporting

patterns.name: Unclear local triggers
patterns.context: Occurs only locally in individual texts; the available samples are insufficient to determine whether there is a stable trigger pattern.
patterns.domain: Business email, papers, websites, and encyclopedias

8_962.description: 主要对英语中的 are（含 ARE）及 have been 结构激活，常见于介绍主体身份、属性或持续状态的句子；其他样本有零散功能词和局部触发，无法确证统一规律。

patterns.name: 系动词 are
patterns.context: 在主语之后作系动词或助动词，尤其是介绍身份、组成、状态或属性时；出现于多种语序中。
patterns.domain: 网页介绍、论坛、百科及普通英文文本

patterns.name: 完成时 have been
patterns.context: 常接状态或持续性描述，如“have been working”；与一般现在时态及公司、机构等主语相邻。
patterns.domain: 公司信息、学术论文及评论文本

patterns.name: 其余英语功能词与句式
patterns.trigger: “and”“since”“until”“when”“to”等未标记词附近的高激活 token
patterns.context: 在流畅英语句子中，这些词与主谓结构、连接或时间表达相邻，但未见统一的独立触发条件。
patterns.domain: 网页、邮件、学术论文、体育报道

patterns.name: 未明的局部触发
patterns.context: 只在个别文本局部出现，现有样本不足以判断是否为稳定触发模式。
patterns.domain: 商务邮件、论文、网页及百科

en.concept: person reference and statement markers in discourse
en.description: The most prominent pattern is first-person pronouns and following statements in emails, especially greetings, team voice, and polite requests in business emails. Activations also occur on several word sequences in game-console commentary, company registration status, and Portuguese parliamentary speeches.

patterns.name: greetings and introductions in business emails
patterns.context: Activates in email openings with a salutation, small talk, and subsequent explanation of the purpose or the sender’s situation.

patterns.name: plural first-person statements in emails
patterns.context: The email body states a position, arrangement, need, or action in the voice of a team or organization; it need not be sentence-initial.

patterns.name: polite requests or responses in formal emails
patterns.context: When expressing thanks, requesting a copy, or confirming the recipient’s proposal, the first-person subject and nearby function words activate.

patterns.name: calls to action and arrangements in organizational announcements
patterns.context: Activates near pronouns and announcement-style wording when announcements, event information, or work updates are shared with organization members.
patterns.domain: Internal corporate announcements or mass emails

patterns.name: game consoles and brand topics
patterns.context: Brand and product names and nearby words activate in discussions of console launches, market performance, or later developments.

patterns.name: business status in company registration descriptions
patterns.context: A company’s activities and status are reported in a descriptive, database-like format in company registrations or business records.

patterns.name: polite expressions in Portuguese parliamentary speeches
patterns.context: A speech is introduced with a formal form of address and uses polite expressions or negative constructions.

8_962.concept: 语篇中的人称与陈述标记
8_962.description: 最突出模式是邮件中的第一人称代词及其后续陈述，尤其商务邮件的问候、团队口吻和礼貌请求。另对游戏主机评论、公司登记状态和葡语议会发言中的若干词串激活。

patterns.name: 商务邮件中的问候与自我介绍
patterns.context: 邮件开头的称呼、寒暄，以及随后介绍来意或自身情况时激活。

patterns.name: 邮件中的复数第一人称陈述
patterns.context: 邮件正文以团队或组织口吻说明立场、安排、需求或行动时；并不要求句首。

patterns.name: 正式邮件中的礼貌请求或回应
patterns.context: 邮件中表达感谢、请求副本或确认对方提议时，第一人称主语及邻近功能词激活。

patterns.name: 组织公告中的号召与安排
patterns.context: 面向组织成员发布公告、活动信息或工作进展时，代词和公告式措辞附近激活。
patterns.domain: 企业内部公告或群发邮件

patterns.name: 游戏主机及品牌话题
patterns.context: 讨论游戏主机发布、市场表现或后续发展时，品牌和产品名及邻近词激活。

patterns.name: 公司登记描述中的经营状态
patterns.context: 公司登记或商业资料以描述性、数据库式格式报告公司活动和状态时。

patterns.name: 葡语议会发言中的礼貌表达
patterns.context: 议会发言中以正式称谓引入发言，并使用礼貌表达或否定结构时。

en.description: All segments show strong activation on the period at the end of a complete declarative sentence, across styles, domains, and meanings; this is primarily interpretable as end-of-sentence punctuation detection.

patterns.name: Sentence-final period
patterns.context: The period appears at the end of a complete declarative sentence, often immediately before a line break or a new sentence; activation is concentrated on the period token.
patterns.domain: Cross-domain email, forum posts, court records, parliamentary speeches, news, and blogs

8_962.description: 所有片段都在完整陈述句的句号处出现强激活，跨文体、领域和句意；主要可解释为句末标点检测。

patterns.name: 句末句号
patterns.context: 句号位于完整陈述句末尾，常紧接换行或新句；激活集中在句号 token。
patterns.domain: 跨领域的邮件、论坛帖子、法院记录、议会发言、新闻及博客

en.description: Activations often occur in supplementary or result clauses introduced by connectives, and also in email politeness requests, greetings asking after someone, formal Polish emphasis, and advertising-style self-introductions; line-break boundaries also activate. The grammatical or formatting regularities shared across these settings are not entirely clear.

patterns.name: relative clause or supplementary explanation after a noun
patterns.context: Highlights often fall on a connective or the beginning of the clause that follows; a person, thing, or situation is introduced first, then elaborated, qualified, or followed by a result.
patterns.domain: News, sports commentary, product reviews, personal introductions, and other prose

patterns.name: polite phrasing in emails
patterns.context: In the body of a business email, after a salutation or subject, the writer expresses thanks, makes a request, or states a courteous follow-up action.

patterns.name: email greeting and asking after someone
patterns.context: An informal email opens by greeting the recipient and then describing the sender’s recent situation.

patterns.name: expressing a personal position in Polish
patterns.context: In formal Polish writing, an expression equivalent to “I would like to emphasize ..., that is ...” occurs; activation centers on the verb ending and following connective structure.

patterns.name: personal-profile statement after a question
patterns.context: In a personal or social advertisement, a title-style question is followed by a first-person introduction of identity and social goals.

patterns.name: paragraph or item boundaries
patterns.context: A newline or blank line marks boundaries between paragraphs, email bodies, headings, or list items; it may contribute to activation, but is not consistent across every passage.

8_962.description: 激活常见于连接词引出的补充或结果从句，也出现在邮件的礼貌请求、问候近况、波兰语正式强调及广告式自我介绍；换行边界亦有激活。各场景共享的语法或格式规律不完全明确。

patterns.name: 名词后接关系从句或补充说明
patterns.trigger: « who»10« have»6« already»3；« that»5« week»3« so»10；« that»5« had»5；« with»2；« so»9
patterns.context: 高亮常落在连接词或其后的从句开头；前面先给出人物、事物或情境，随后补充说明、限定或交代结果。
patterns.domain: 新闻、体育评论、产品评测、个人介绍和其他散文

patterns.name: 邮件中的礼貌句式
patterns.trigger: «I»6« enjoyed»2 your presentation ...«.»10«↵»4«I»6« would»1 appreciate；«Can»3 you please provide me with
patterns.context: 商务邮件正文中，称呼或主题之后表达感谢、请求或客气的后续动作。

patterns.name: 邮件问候与近况
patterns.trigger: «Hi»3« Kay»3« how»5« are»2« you»2«!»7« I»6« have»4« been»5；« I»7« just»4 started
patterns.context: 非正式邮件开头先问候收件人，再介绍自己的近况。

patterns.name: 波兰语句中强调个人立场
patterns.context: 波兰语正式论述中出现相当于“我想强调……，即/那……”的表达；激活集中在动词词尾及后续连接结构。

patterns.name: 问句后的个人资料陈述
patterns.trigger: «Just»2 looking for some good times«?»2«↵»1«↵»1«I»4« am»3 23 year old
patterns.context: 个人交友或社交广告中，标题式问句后转入第一人称身份和交友需求介绍。

patterns.name: 段落或条目边界
patterns.context: 换行或空行标记出现在段落、邮件正文、标题或列表条目之间；本身可能贡献激活，但并非每段都一致。

en.description: Highly sensitive primarily to «chciałbym» (“I would like...”) in Polish formal speeches; also responds to sentence-initial English first-person «I» in emails or articles, and once to the relative pronoun «who» in sports reporting.

patterns.name: Polish first-person desiderative parenthetical
patterns.context: In a formal speech, the speaker uses “I would like...” to introduce a statement, thanks, or emphasis; some samples are preceded by sentence-final punctuation or occur at the beginning of a paragraph

patterns.name: English email salutation or body opening
patterns.context: The greeting or beginning of the body after the email header (To/Cc/Subject), or a sentence immediately following the salutation

patterns.name: English sentence-initial pronoun I
patterns.context: The start of a first-person sentence in non-email text; no clear, consistent semantic collocation

patterns.name: English relative pronoun who
patterns.context: A sports story first mentions the team County, then uses a relative clause to describe its existing player changes

8_962.concept: 句首第一人称/话语引入
8_962.description: 主要对波兰语正式演讲中的«chciałbym»（“我想……”）高度敏感；另对邮件或文章中句首英文第一人称«I»有反应，并有一次体育报道关系代词«who»激活。

patterns.name: 波兰语第一人称愿望式插入语
patterns.context: 正式发言中说话者以“我想……”引出陈述、致谢或强调；部分样本前有句末标点或段落开头

patterns.name: 英文邮件称呼或正文开头
patterns.trigger: «I»；常见于称呼之后的«I enjoyed»、«I would appreciate»，或邮件正文起始
patterns.context: 邮件头部（To/Cc/Subject）之后的问候、正文开头，或紧随称呼后的句子

patterns.name: 英文句首代词 I
patterns.context: 非邮件文本中第一人称句子开头；没有明显统一的语义搭配

patterns.name: 英文关系代词 who
patterns.context: 体育新闻中先提及球队 County，再以关系从句描述其已有的球员变动

en.concept: Discourse organization and turn initiation at sentence/paragraph openings
en.description: Strongly responds to first-person expressions such as Polish parliamentary «chciałbym»; also sensitive to email salutations, fields, polite thanks, and English sentence-initial personal pronouns. It also covers news relative clauses, business self-introductions, and work reports.

patterns.name: Polish first-person speech formula
patterns.context: In Polish sentences, the speaker uses the first person to express “I would like to…”, often at the beginning of a parliamentary speech paragraph or at a transition; activation concentrates on «-bym» and nearby words.

patterns.name: Email greetings and salutations
patterns.context: At the head of an email or beginning of its body, a salutation is followed by a line break and then a polite greeting, thanks, or request.
patterns.domain: Enron emails and business email text

patterns.name: English sentence-initial personal pronouns
patterns.context: Personal pronouns at the beginning of a sentence or clause; seen in email bodies and in clauses introduced by relative pronouns in news sentences.

patterns.name: Email headers and field formatting
patterns.context: Structured separation between email metadata and body, often immediately following the recipient’s salutation or preceding the body.

patterns.name: English politeness, gratitude, or positive evaluation
patterns.context: Expressing thanks, appreciation, or a positive attitude in business correspondence; often at the beginning of an email body or in a reply.

patterns.name: Relative clauses in news narration
patterns.context: In a news sentence, who introduces supplementary information about a previously mentioned team or organization.

patterns.name: Self-introduction in business pitches
patterns.context: In a business proposal or service introduction, a sentence beginning with We describes the team’s identity or expertise; preceding text discusses services, the company, or a quote.

patterns.name: Completed tasks in English business narration
patterns.context: Using the first person to report a negotiation or work task just completed.

8_962.concept: 句首／段首的话语组织与发言启动
8_962.description: 强烈响应波兰议会发言中「chciałbym」式第一人称表达；另对邮件称呼、字段、礼貌致谢及英语句首人称代词等结构敏感，也覆盖新闻关系从句和商务自我介绍、工作汇报。

patterns.name: 波兰语第一人称发言公式
patterns.trigger: 「chciałbym」及其分词形式（如「chciałbym podkreślić」「chciałbym powiedzieć」「chciałbym zwrócić uwagę」「chciałbym podziękować」）
patterns.context: 波兰语句子中，发言者以第一人称表达“我想……”，常出现在议会演讲的段落开头或转折处；激活集中在「-bym」及邻近词语。

patterns.name: 邮件问候与称呼
patterns.context: 邮件头部或正文开头，称呼后换行，再进入礼貌问候、致谢或请求。
patterns.domain: Enron 邮件及商业邮件文本

patterns.name: 英语句首人称代词
patterns.context: 句子或从句开头的人称代词；可见于邮件正文，也见于新闻句中关系代词引出的从句。
patterns.domain: 英语邮件与新闻／网页文本

patterns.name: 邮件头部与字段格式
patterns.context: 邮件元数据与正文之间的结构化分隔，常紧接收件人称呼或正文。

patterns.name: 英语礼貌、感谢或正面评价
patterns.trigger: 「Thanks for your help」「I enjoyed your presentation」「I am delighted and thankful」
patterns.context: 商务往来中表达感谢、赞赏或积极态度；常处于邮件正文开头或回应处。

patterns.name: 新闻叙述中的关系从句
patterns.context: 新闻句中以 who 引出关于前述球队或组织的补充说明。

patterns.name: 商务推介中的自我介绍
patterns.context: 商业提案或服务介绍中以 We 开头，说明团队身份或专长；前文谈及服务、公司或报价。

patterns.name: 英语商务叙述中的完成事项
patterns.context: 以第一人称报告刚完成的谈判或工作事项。

en.description: Three Polish formal speeches jointly activate “chciałbym/chciałabym” (I would like...); five English personal narratives activate on so, often introducing a result, reaction, or decision. Email also activates most strongly on so; technical Q&A activates on self-description elements such as Hi/i am/I have, which are difficult to unify with the first two patterns.

patterns.name: Polish polite-speech formula
patterns.context: In Polish formal or parliamentary speeches, the first-person conditional “I would like...” introduces content to emphasize or add; activation covers «chciałbym/chciałabym» and the following material.

patterns.name: Concessive or causal progression after so
patterns.context: In English narratives, so introduces a result, explanation, subsequent action, or attitude after a turn; the preceding text often describes a cause or background, and the following text gives an evaluation, reaction, or decision.
patterns.domain: Pile-CC personal narratives, experience sharing, and forum text

patterns.name: Polite request/thanks context in English email
patterns.context: In business email, the sender first explains the recipient's schedule or inconvenience, then uses so to introduce the sender's reaction (especially thanks); the highlight falls on so rather than a stable content word.

patterns.name: Self-introduction in English technical Q&A
patterns.context: The questioner introduces themself as a beginner and describes what they have already configured; there is no Polish formula or clear so trigger.

8_962.description: 三段波兰语正式发言共同激活“chciałbym/chciałabym”（我想……）；五段英语个人叙述在 so 处激活，常接结果、反应或决定。邮件亦在 so 处最强；技术问答则激活于 Hi/i am/I have 等自述成分，难与前两类统一。

patterns.name: 波兰语礼貌发言公式
patterns.context: 波兰语正式演讲或议会发言中，第一人称条件式“我想……”引出要强调或补充的内容；激活覆盖「chciałbym/chciałabym」及其后续部分。

patterns.name: so 后的让步或因果推进
patterns.context: 英语叙述中 so 引出结果、解释、转折后的后续行动或态度；其前文常描述原因或背景，后文接评价、反应或决定。
patterns.domain: Pile-CC 个人叙述、经验分享与论坛文本

patterns.name: 英文邮件中的礼貌请求/致谢语境
patterns.context: 商务邮件里先交代对方行程或不便，再用 so 引出说话者的反应（特别感谢）；高亮落在 so，而非某个稳定的内容词。

patterns.name: 英语技术问答的自我介绍
patterns.context: 提问者以新手身份介绍自己并陈述已完成的设置；没有出现波兰语公式或明显的 so 触发词。

en.description: The most stable trigger pattern is the Polish conditional first-person “chciałbym” (“I would like”) in formal speeches, often introducing a statement, emphasis, thanks, or address. Other paragraphs sporadically contain English first-person contractions, personal pronouns, and forum greetings, with no consistent word form.

patterns.name: Polish conditional first-person polite speech
patterns.context: In formal Polish speeches, often followed by verbs such as “podkreślić”, “zwrócić uwagę”, “powiedzieć”, “powitać”, or “podziękować”; means “I would like to…” and often occurs at the beginning or conclusion of a speech.

patterns.name: English conditional first-person contraction
patterns.context: A first-person contraction appears in conversational English statements; paragraph 3 is a personal description of golf performance, and paragraph 7 is a chat about getting help with Ubuntu.

patterns.name: Pronouns and narration in English emails
patterns.context: The email body uses first and second person to narrate communications or business matters; it does not show the specific word form found in the Polish pattern.

patterns.name: Forum greeting
patterns.context: The body of a technical forum post opens with a greeting to the community; its specific trigger word differs from those in other paragraphs.

8_962.description: 最稳定的触发模式是波兰语正式讲话中的第一人称条件式“chciałbym”（我想），常引出发言、强调、致谢或致辞。其他段落零散出现英语第一人称缩写、人称代词及论坛问候，未见统一词形。

patterns.name: 波兰语条件式第一人称礼貌发言
patterns.context: 在波兰语正式发言中，常接“podkreślić”“zwrócić uwagę”“powiedzieć”“powitać”“podziękować”等动词；表示“我想……”，且多位于讲话开头或总结处。

patterns.name: 英语条件式第一人称缩写
patterns.context: 英语口语式陈述中出现第一人称缩写；第3段是对高尔夫球表现的个人描述，第7段是聊天中的 Ubuntu 求助对话。
patterns.domain: 论坛/在线聊天及个人经验叙述

patterns.name: 英语邮件中的人称与叙述语
patterns.context: 邮件正文中以第一、第二人称叙述联络或商业事项；不呈现与波兰语模式相同的具体词形。

patterns.name: 论坛问候语
patterns.context: 技术论坛帖子正文以面向社区的问候开场；与其他段落的具体触发词不同。

en.description: Activations span multiple languages and styles, appearing mainly in English first-person online narratives, causal so, novice technical questions, and line-break boundaries. They also cover German and Polish parliamentary subword fragments, business email, golf reviews, and life experiences, with no single semantic pattern apparent.

patterns.name: so after causal or contrastive linking
patterns.context: Connects a preceding situation with a following result, judgment, or question; in [1][2][10] it occurs within a local sentence, and in [7] it appears in an informal question explanation.
patterns.domain: Online text, forums, or Q&A text

patterns.name: First-person I and colloquial contractions
patterns.context: In first-person narration, questions, or email, usually when describing personal experience, knowledge level, actions, or requests.
patterns.domain: Forum Q&A, email, personal online posts

patterns.name: English perfect tense and been
patterns.context: have/'ve been follows a first-person subject to describe an ongoing state or recent experience.

patterns.name: Sentence-initial line-break marker
patterns.context: A line-break boundary in a paragraph, question, or email body; it may be a formatting boundary rather than a lexical-semantic trigger.

patterns.name: StackExchange novice-question template
patterns.context: In a question marked Q:, the questioner says they are unfamiliar with the technical topic, then asks a question or seeks help.

patterns.name: German function words and within-word fragments
patterns.context: In continuous German sentences, activation falls on words, subword fragments, and common function words; the context discusses media patterns and European characteristics.

patterns.name: Polish within-word fragments and first-person expression
patterns.context: In Polish parliamentary sentences, activation is scattered across within-word subword fragments; the first-person expression «Chciałbym» and an emphasis context appear.

patterns.name: Polite thanks and meeting invitation in email
patterns.context: An email thanks someone for accepting an invitation to speak at a meeting, explains the schedule, and expresses gratitude.

patterns.name: Conditional outcome in golf review
patterns.context: Describes firm course greens and uses so to introduce the result that the ball does not stop quickly; a distance-comparison review context also appears.

patterns.name: Engineer father and silicone spray
patterns.context: First discusses cleaning weatherstripping, then mentions that the speaker's father previously worked in aerospace and automotive industries, and silicone spray appears.

8_962.description: 激活横跨多语种与多文体，主要见于英语第一人称网络叙述、因果 so、新手技术提问和换行边界；也覆盖德波议会词片段、商务邮件、高尔夫评测及生活经验，未见单一语义模式。

patterns.name: 因果或转折连接词后的 so
patterns.context: 连接前面的情况与后面的结果、判断或提问；在[1][2][10]中位于局部句中，在[7]中位于口语化提问说明中。
patterns.domain: 网络文本、论坛或问答文本

patterns.name: 第一人称 I 及其口语缩写
patterns.context: 第一人称叙述、提问或邮件中；通常在描述个人经历、知识水平、行动或请求。
patterns.domain: 论坛问答、邮件、个人网络发言

patterns.name: 英语完成时与 been
patterns.context: 第一人称主语后出现 have/'ve been，描述持续状态或近期经历。

patterns.name: 句首换行标记
patterns.context: 段落、问题或邮件正文的换行边界；本身可能是格式边界而非词汇语义触发。
patterns.domain: 网页文本、StackExchange 问答、邮件

patterns.name: StackExchange 新手提问模板
patterns.context: Q: 标记的问题中，提问者自述对技术主题不熟悉，随后提出问题或寻求帮助。

patterns.name: 德语句中功能词及词内片段
patterns.context: 德语连续句子中，激活落在词、词片段及常见功能词上；语境讨论媒体模式与欧洲特点。

patterns.name: 波兰语词内片段及第一人称表达
patterns.context: 波兰语议会句子中，激活分散在词内子词片段；出现第一人称表达«Chciałbym»及强调语境。

patterns.name: 邮件礼貌致谢与会议邀请
patterns.context: 邮件中感谢对方接受会议发言邀请，并说明时间安排、表达感谢。

patterns.name: 高尔夫球评测中的条件结果
patterns.context: 描述球场果岭条件较硬，并以 so 引出球难以快速停下的结果；另有距离比较的评测语境。

patterns.name: 工程师父亲与硅胶喷剂
patterns.context: 先谈门封条清洁，再提及父亲曾从事航空航天和汽车行业，并出现硅胶喷剂。

en.concept: Syntactic cohesion and common function words
en.description: Activations are distributed across languages and genres, involving inter-sentence linking, first-person statements, punctuation, and a few modal expressions, email instructions, and subword fragments within words; no single stable semantic theme is apparent.

patterns.name: Judgment following a concessive or causal connector
patterns.context: Connects preceding and following clauses, often in sentences expressing cause, contrast, or result; typically involves a connector near the marked token and the judgment that follows.
patterns.domain: English web pages, reviews, or blogs

patterns.name: First-person pronoun and following verb
patterns.context: An opinion, experience, plan, or judgment follows a first-person subject; in some cases, «it» also appears in a result or prediction sentence.
patterns.domain: English web pages and informal blogs

patterns.name: Punctuation at the end of a sentence or phrase
patterns.context: Punctuation occurs at the end of a sentence or heading; it may also co-occur with a preceding connector and sentence boundary.
patterns.domain: English web pages, formal writing, and email

patterns.name: German modal judgment
patterns.context: Expresses the speaker’s opinion or possibility, appearing after “Meiner Ansicht nach”.

patterns.name: German explanatory clause connector
patterns.context: Introduces a cause or explanation, following an evaluation of the European model.

patterns.name: Portuguese stance and claim expression
patterns.context: Occurs in sentences expressing a political stance, commitment, or personal opinion.

patterns.name: Polite request language in email
patterns.context: Introduces an instruction asking the recipient to take action in an approval notification email.

patterns.name: Speaker tag after quoted content
patterns.context: A quotation mark opens a direct quote, followed by a statement about a product’s popularity.

patterns.name: Non-English subword fragments within words
patterns.context: These are internal fragments of Portuguese and German words, respectively; the word meanings where they activate are not consistent, and they lack a shared local context.

8_962.concept: 句法衔接与常见功能词
8_962.description: 激活分散在多种语言和文体中，涉及句间连接、第一人称陈述、标点及少数情态、邮件指令和词内子词片段；未见稳定的单一语义主题。

patterns.name: 让步或因果连接后的判断
patterns.context: 连接前后分句，常出现在表达原因、转折或结果的句子中；多为被标记 token 附近的连接词及其后续判断。

patterns.name: 第一人称代词及后续动词
patterns.context: 第一人称主语后接观点、经历、计划或判断；个别情况下 «it» 也出现在结果或预测句中。
patterns.domain: 英语网页及非正式博客

patterns.name: 句末或短语末的标点
patterns.context: 标点位于句子或标题末尾；也可能与前面的连接词、句子边界共同出现。
patterns.domain: 英语网页、正式文体及邮件

patterns.name: 德语情态判断
patterns.context: 表达说话者观点或可能性，出现在“Meiner Ansicht nach”之后。

patterns.name: 德语解释性从句连接
patterns.context: 引出原因或解释，前接对欧洲模式的评价。

patterns.name: 葡语立场与主张表达
patterns.context: 处于表达政治立场、承诺或个人观点的句子中。

patterns.name: 邮件请求礼貌用语
patterns.context: 审批通知邮件中，引出要求收件人采取操作的指令。
patterns.domain: 企业内部自动通知邮件

patterns.name: 引述内容后的说话人标记
patterns.context: 引号开启直接引述，后接关于产品受欢迎程度的说法。

patterns.name: 非英语词内子词片段
patterns.context: 分别是葡语、德语词的内部切分片段；激活所在词义并不统一，缺少共同局部语境。

en.description: Activations are scattered across multilingual text: English first-person narratives and coordination, Portuguese or German fragments in parliamentary speeches, and several local word fragments without clear commonalities. There is no single reliable trigger pattern yet.

patterns.name: English first-person experience and narration
patterns.context: An English narrative contains a first-person subject, especially when discussing personal experience, plans, opinions, or progress; activation is distributed across different words, with no single consistent trigger word.
patterns.domain: English forum, blog, and news text

patterns.name: English and introducing coordination or additional information
patterns.context: Connects phrases or clauses, with the following text adding information; found in English news, reviews, and narratives.

patterns.name: Expressing views in European Parliament speeches
patterns.context: Parliamentary speeches state a position or evaluate the parliament or policy; these passages are primarily in Portuguese or German, but the specific marked fragments vary.

patterns.name: Portuguese relative pronouns and linking expressions
patterns.context: Common function words appear in Portuguese formal statements or technical explanations; activation may depend on segmented subword fragments and local syntactic context.
patterns.domain: Portuguese parliamentary speeches and technical Q&A

patterns.name: German within-word fragments and endings
patterns.context: In German parliamentary text, marked elements fall on complete words or subword fragments, without forming a clear, consistent syntactic pattern.

patterns.name: Unclustered local markers
patterns.context: Each occurs in different languages, topics, and syntactic positions; these segments alone are insufficient to establish a shared trigger condition.
patterns.domain: Sports news, job forums, technical Q&A, business reviews, and parliamentary text

8_962.description: 激活分散于多语种文本：英语第一人称叙述及并列连接、议会发言中的葡语或德语片段，以及若干无明确共性的局部词片。尚无单一可靠触发模式。

patterns.name: 英语第一人称经历与叙述
patterns.context: 英语叙述中出现第一人称主语，尤其是在讲个人经历、计划、看法或进展时；激活分布在不同词上，未见统一的单一触发词。
patterns.domain: 论坛、博客及新闻类英语文本

patterns.name: 英语后接并列或补充内容的 and
patterns.context: 连接短语或分句，后文继续补充信息；见于英语新闻、评论和叙述。

patterns.name: 欧洲议会发言中的观点表达
patterns.context: 议会发言中陈述立场、评价议会或政策；这些段落以葡萄牙语或德语为主，但被标记的具体碎片并不一致。

patterns.name: 葡语中的关系代词及连接表达
patterns.context: 葡语正式陈述或技术说明中出现常见功能词；激活可能依赖被拆分的词片及局部句法上下文。
patterns.domain: 葡语议会发言及技术问答

patterns.name: 德语词内片段与词尾
patterns.trigger: «st»（lässt 的词尾片段）、«es»（Dies 的词内片段）、«da»
patterns.context: 德语议会文本中，标记落在完整词或子词片段上，未形成明确一致的句法模式。

patterns.name: 未能归并的局部标记
patterns.context: 各自出现在不同语种、主题和句法位置；仅凭这些片段无法确认共同触发条件。
patterns.domain: 体育新闻、求职论坛、技术问答、商业评论及议会文本

en.description: Across multilingual examples, activations often involve finite verbs, auxiliaries, or copulas: German hat/muss, English had/are, and Portuguese é, among others. There is also I and several within-word fragments, with triggers that are not fully consistent.

patterns.name: English past-perfect have
patterns.context: In English, have functions as an auxiliary to form the past perfect or express having already owned or experienced something; it is followed by a past participle or object.

patterns.name: German third-person singular present perfect
patterns.context: In German sentences, the verb occurs in a finite clause or main clause; several instances are sentence-initial or in subordinate clauses with “hat”, and there is also the modal verb “muss”.

patterns.name: Portuguese third-person/plural verb forms
patterns.context: In Portuguese sentences, activation falls on verb forms licensed by the subject or clause structure; these may be “é” or a within-word fragment of “estou”.
patterns.domain: EuroParl Portuguese speech and StackExchange code discussion

patterns.name: English copula be
patterns.context: The copula follows the English plural subject “They” and is followed by an identity description.

patterns.name: English first-person subject
patterns.context: Occurs in first-person statements or questions, in structures such as “I am” and “I was”.

patterns.name: Verb fragments within tokenized words
patterns.context: Activation may cover internal fragments of verbs split by tokenization rather than whole words; the observed fragments belong to Portuguese “permanece” and “estou” and German “bereits”, the latter not clearly being a verb.

8_962.description: 多语种样例中常激活有限动词、助动词或系词：德语hat/muss，英语had/are及葡语é等；另有I和若干词内片段，触发并不完全一致。

patterns.name: 英语过去完成式 have
patterns.trigger: "had"；特别是 “it seemed … so it …” 附近的 “had”
patterns.context: 英语中 have 作助动词，构成过去完成式或表达已经拥有、经历；词后接过去分词或宾语。

patterns.name: 德语第三人称单数现在完成式
patterns.context: 德语句中动词位于有限从句或主句中；多处是句首或从句结构中的“hat”，也有情态动词“muss”。

patterns.name: 葡萄牙语第三人称/复数动词形式
patterns.context: 葡萄牙语句中，激活落在由主语或从句结构许可的动词形式上；可能是“é”或“estou”的词内片段。
patterns.domain: EuroParl 葡萄牙语发言及 StackExchange 代码讨论

patterns.name: 英语系词 be
patterns.context: 英语复数主语 “They” 后的系词，后接身份描述。

patterns.name: 英语第一人称主语
patterns.context: 第一人称陈述或提问中，出现在 “I am”“I was”等结构里。

patterns.name: 切分后落在词内的动词片段
patterns.context: 激活可能覆盖经过分词切分的动词内部片段，而非完整词；可见片段分别属于葡萄牙语“permanece”“estou”和德语“bereits”，其中后者并非明确的动词。
patterns.domain: 多语种议会文本与论坛文本

en.description: Activation is particularly prominent on German hat in parliamentary text, and also appears on German Sie, English I/They/you/we/her, and Portuguese que, among other pronouns or function words. Samples span multiple languages and styles, with no single stable trigger pattern; some activations may relate to local lexical or syntactic properties, but remain difficult to explain.

patterns.name: hat in German parliamentary sentences
patterns.context: In a German sentence, hat follows the subject and is followed by a participle, noun, or other syntactic constituent; strong activation falls on hat.

patterns.name: hat in a purpose construction
patterns.context: A German policy proposal precedes it, followed by a purpose expression such as “zum Ziel”; hat activates here, but less strongly than in the first two examples.

patterns.name: English subject I
patterns.context: In English first-person narratives or email, I occurs at the beginning of a sentence or clause, often followed by am, was, 'm, or had.

patterns.name: English plural subject they
patterns.context: In an English quotation, sentence-initial They is followed by are and introduces players and their experience.

patterns.name: German personal pronoun Sie
patterns.context: In German parliamentary speeches, Sie addresses the listener and occurs at the beginning of a sentence or subordinate clause.

patterns.name: English contact and reference words
patterns.context: Second-person, first-person, and object pronouns in English narratives or quotations; their syntactic positions are not entirely consistent.
patterns.domain: Forum posts, email, and sports reporting

patterns.name: Portuguese coordinating conjunction que
patterns.context: In a Portuguese parliamentary sentence, connects a subordinate clause, with o preceding it and a verb phrase following it.

patterns.name: Other pronouns and function words without a clear pattern
patterns.context: Articles, pronouns, or linking elements in German passages; the samples do not establish a consistent trigger word or fixed syntactic condition.
patterns.domain: EuroParl, German and Portuguese parliamentary records

patterns.name: They in an English quotation
patterns.context: A sentence-initial pronoun refers to players mentioned earlier, followed by a description of their international match experience.

8_962.description: 激活较突出地落在德语议会文本的 hat，也出现在德语 Sie、英语 I/They/you/we/her 及葡萄牙语 que 等代词或功能词上。样本跨多语种与文体，未显示单一稳定触发模式；部分激活或与局部词法句法有关，仍难解释。

patterns.name: 德语议会语句中的 hat
patterns.context: 德语句子中，hat 位于主语之后，后接分词、名词或其他句法成分；强激活落在 hat。

patterns.name: 带目的结构中的 hat
patterns.context: 前文为德语政策提案，后接“zum Ziel”等目的表达；此处激活 hat，但强度低于前两例。

patterns.name: 英语主语 I
patterns.context: 英语第一人称叙述或邮件中，I 出现在句首或分句开头，常接 am、was、'm 或 had。

patterns.name: 英语复数主语 they
patterns.context: 英语引述中，句首 They 后接 are，介绍球员及其经历。

patterns.name: 德语人称代词 Sie
patterns.context: 德语议会发言中以 Sie 称呼对方，位于句首或从句开头。

patterns.name: 英语联系与指代词
patterns.context: 英语叙述或引语中的第二、第一人称及宾语代词；具体句法位置不完全一致。
patterns.domain: 论坛帖、邮件与体育报道

patterns.name: 葡萄牙语并列连接词 que
patterns.context: 葡萄牙语议会句子中连接从句，前接 o，后接动词短语。

patterns.name: 无明显统一的其他代词与功能词
patterns.trigger: « es»1、« den»1、« die»1、« sich»2、« das»2、« quando/que»等局部上下文成分
patterns.context: 德语段落中的冠词、代词或连接成分；没有一致的触发词或固定句法条件可从样本确认。
patterns.domain: EuroParl，德语及葡萄牙语议会记录

patterns.name: 英语引述中的 They
patterns.context: 句首代词指代前文提及的球员，后续描述其国际比赛经验。

en.description: Activations are distributed across different languages and contexts: German “hat” recurs, alongside Portuguese “que”, English “so” and “and”, and occasional content words. Apart from “hat”, no stable shared trigger condition is apparent.

patterns.name: German auxiliary “hat”
patterns.context: Occurs in German declarative sentences, followed by a subject or other sentence elements; in the examples shown, it is a perfect auxiliary or a verb meaning “have/aim at”.

patterns.name: Portuguese clause connector “que”
patterns.context: Occurs in Portuguese parliamentary speech, linking clauses; here it appears in the structure “penso que te…”.

patterns.name: “so” and its surrounding context
patterns.context: Used to indicate degree or result in English narration; the strong activation position is not fully consistent.

patterns.name: Coordinating conjunction “and”
patterns.context: Connects two noun phrases in English narration, followed by “the car industry”.

patterns.name: Other locally high-activation words
patterns.context: These occur respectively in an email sentence about a holiday and a Portuguese parliamentary speech sentence about a stance; no shared syntactic or semantic condition is apparent.
patterns.domain: Enron emails; EuroParl Portuguese parliamentary speech

8_962.description: 激活分散在不同语言和语境：德语“hat”反复出现，另有葡语“que”、英语“so”“and”及个别内容词；除“hat”外未见稳定共同触发条件。

patterns.name: 德语助动词“hat”
patterns.context: 出现在德语陈述句中，后接主语或其他句子成分；在所示句子里是完成时助动词或表示“有/以……为目标”的动词。

patterns.name: 葡语从句连接词“que”
patterns.context: 出现在葡语议会发言中，连接前后分句；此处位于“penso que te…”结构中。

patterns.name: “so”及其邻近语境
patterns.context: 英语叙述中的程度或结果用法；强激活位置并不完全一致。

patterns.name: 并列连词“and”
patterns.context: 英语叙述中连接两个名词短语，后接“the car industry”。

patterns.name: 其他局部高激活词
patterns.context: 分别出现在邮件中关于节日的句子、葡语议会发言中关于立场的句子；看不出共同句法或语义条件。
patterns.domain: Enron 邮件；EuroParl 葡语议会发言

en.description: Activations occur mainly on sentence-final punctuation, contrast or result expressions, and thank-yous or reply boundaries in emails and Q&A. They also appear in suggestions, positive evaluations, and ordinary narratives on varied topics, with no single stable semantic trigger.

patterns.name: Sentence-final thanks or response
patterns.context: Thanking someone before ending a passage, or politely closing a Q&A post; activation falls on a period or a marker adjacent to the thanks.

patterns.name: Sentence-final contrast or conclusion marker
patterns.context: When a narrative or argument advances to a result, time range, or subsequent state; activation concentrates near “so” or sentence-final punctuation.

patterns.name: Introducing specific advice or explanation
patterns.context: A Q&A reply gives practical advice or factual information, often followed by a specific explanation or version details.

patterns.name: Polite Q&A format at text boundaries
patterns.context: At the reply boundary of an email body or Q&A post, with a salutation, blank line, or formatting marker such as “A:” nearby.

patterns.name: Positive evaluation or endorsement
patterns.context: Positively evaluating or supporting a product, institution, experience, or political position.
patterns.domain: Encyclopedias, online discussions, Portuguese speeches in the European Parliament

patterns.name: Proper nouns or localized multilingual activation
patterns.context: In Portuguese political text, activation is scattered within or between words; no clear syntactic trigger shared with other passages is apparent.

patterns.name: Sporadic activations in narratives on varied topics
patterns.context: Ordinary narratives about personal experiences, institutional introductions, sports interviews, or parenting discussions; marked positions have no stable shared trigger substring.
patterns.domain: Web articles, encyclopedias, sports and parenting discussions

8_962.description: 激活多见于句末标点、转折或结果表达，以及邮件和问答中的致谢、回复边界；也出现在建议、肯定评价和多种主题的普通叙述中，未见单一稳定语义触发条件。

patterns.name: 句末致谢或回应
patterns.trigger: [2] “Thank you very much for your data.”；[5] “Thank you everyone for your suggestions.”；[9] “Thanks”
patterns.context: 感谢对方后结束一段话，或作为问答帖中的礼貌收尾；激活落在句号或与致谢相邻的标记上。

patterns.name: 句末转折或结论标记
patterns.trigger: [1] “so that put a swift end to that dream”；[6] “so far”；[8] “and have had”；[10] “so I’m just waiting”
patterns.context: 叙述或论述推进到结果、时间范围或后续状态时；激活集中在“so”附近或句末标点。

patterns.name: 引出具体建议或说明
patterns.trigger: [3] “Try changing it, e.g.”；[9] “The documentation on bitcoin.org is currently out of date.”
patterns.context: 问答回复中给出操作建议或事实说明，常接具体解释、版本信息。

patterns.name: 文本边界处的礼貌问答格式
patterns.trigger: [2] “Subject: Re: Weather and energy price Data”；[5] “A: Thank you everyone”
patterns.context: 邮件正文或问答帖的回复边界，周围有称呼、空行或“A:”等格式标记。

patterns.name: 肯定性评价或认可
patterns.trigger: [4] “seemed only natural”；[6] “it’s excellent”；[7] “o nosso grupo político apoia o nosso compromisso”
patterns.context: 对产品、机构、经验或政治主张作正面评价或表示支持。
patterns.domain: 百科、网络讨论、欧洲议会葡萄牙语发言

patterns.name: 专名或多语种局部激活
patterns.trigger: [7] “humanitária a Gaza através do mecanismo internacional”
patterns.context: 葡萄牙语政治文本中，激活分散在词内或词间；未见与其他段共享的明确句法触发条件。
patterns.domain: 欧洲议会葡萄牙语文本

patterns.name: 多主题口语叙述中的零散激活
patterns.trigger: [1] “Garrett”；[4] “Carnegie Mellon”；[8] “international players”；[10] “girls tend to potty train earlier than boys”
patterns.context: 个人经历、机构介绍、体育访谈或育儿讨论中的普通叙述；所标记位置没有稳定共同触发子串。
patterns.domain: 网络文章、百科、体育与育儿讨论

en.description: Activations most consistently cluster around positions that introduce supplementary information, explanations, or clauses in multilingual formal speeches, especially near que and German und/dass. They also accompany local patterns involving first-person speech, turn boundaries, and numerical explanations. Paragraph 9 is a Portuguese comment after webpage code; its local word-position similarity does not establish a shared cause with the parliamentary pattern.

patterns.name: Result-introducing “que” in conditional or causal explanations
patterns.context: Activation often falls on a clause introducer or an adjacent phrase; in Portuguese, it commonly occurs in parliamentary speech structures such as “gostaria de salientar ... que existe” and “porque tive ...”; German passages also show it near “und ich ...” and “dass mir ...”.
patterns.domain: Primarily formal multilingual European Parliament speeches, with some StackExchange Portuguese text

patterns.name: First-person expression in parliamentary speech
patterns.context: Occurs when a speaker expresses intent, views, thanks, or personal circumstances, often near a first-person pronoun, modal verb, or verb phrase.
patterns.domain: Formal debates and chair’s remarks in EuroParl

patterns.name: Turn-taking, chair address, and line-break boundaries
patterns.context: Near parliamentary speaker salutations, chair responses, or the beginning of a new turn; some activations fall on line breaks or sentence-initial formatting tokens.

patterns.name: Numerical and monetary statistics
patterns.context: After a numerical comparison involving amounts and years, “Querer isto dizer que...” introduces an explanation or summary of a trend.

patterns.name: Portuguese comments near code strings and webpage markup
patterns.context: A Portuguese comment, “observe bem o meu código-fonte”, appears after webpage code or HTML; strong activation falls on “que” and nearby positions, with a local token form different from the parliamentary passages.
patterns.domain: StackExchange questions and answers with mixed code/HTML

patterns.name: Local word-form fragments in multilingual parliamentary text
patterns.context: Tokenized fragments from different languages are scattered across Portuguese, Italian, and German speeches; apart from occurring in formal speech, they show no consistent word-form or semantic trigger condition.

8_962.concept: 正式文本中的从句衔接
8_962.description: 激活最稳定地集中在多语种正式发言里引出补充、解释或从句的连接位置，尤其是que及德语und/dass附近；还伴随第一人称发言、轮次边界、数字说明等局部模式。第9段是网页代码后的葡语评论，只有局部词位相似，无法确定与议会模式同因。

patterns.name: 条件句或原因说明中的结果引出词“que”
patterns.context: 激活常落在从句引导词或相邻短语上；在葡萄牙语中常见于“gostaria de salientar ... que existe”“porque tive ...”等议会发言句式；德语段也出现在“und ich ...”“dass mir ...”附近。
patterns.domain: 以欧洲议会多语种正式发言为主，另有 StackExchange 葡萄牙语文本

patterns.name: 议会发言中的第一人称表达
patterns.trigger: « ich»7、« mir»3、« möchte»6、« gostaria»6、« quero»4、« penso»3
patterns.context: 发言者表达意愿、看法、感谢或说明自身处境时出现，常位于第一人称代词、情态动词或动词短语附近。
patterns.domain: EuroParl 的正式辩论与主席发言

patterns.name: 发言轮次、主席称呼及换行边界
patterns.context: 议会发言者称呼、主席回应或新发言轮次起始附近；部分激活落在换行或句首格式 token 上。

patterns.name: 数字与金额统计表述
patterns.context: 金额和年份构成的数值比较后，接“Querer isto dizer que...”引出解释或趋势总结。

patterns.name: 口袋代码字符串及网页标记附近的葡语评论
patterns.context: 网页代码或 HTML 片段之后出现葡语评论“observe bem o meu código-fonte”；强激活落在“que”及其邻近位置，局部 token 形态与议会段落不同。
patterns.domain: StackExchange 问答及代码/HTML 混排

patterns.name: 多语种议会文本中的局部词形碎片
patterns.context: 不同语言的分词片段散布在葡语、意大利语、德语发言中；除同处于正式发言语境外，未见统一的词形或语义触发条件。

en.concept: Statements and transitions in formal discourse
en.description: Occurs mainly in formal speeches in the European Parliament, involving speaker positions, procedure, or policy argumentation; also appears in Q&A openings and email apologies. Strong activations span languages and syntactic positions, making them difficult to attribute to a single word form.

patterns.name: Transition to first-person statements in parliamentary speeches
patterns.context: Many activations occur in parliamentary speeches, especially at the beginning of a sentence or new paragraph when the speaker states a position, evaluates, explains, or addresses the audience; [1] also appears within a sentence on «ich» and related words.
patterns.domain: Formal European Parliament debates, primarily German

patterns.name: Thanks and apologies in formal parliamentary speeches
patterns.context: In an Italian speech, thanking Parliament for its contribution before moving to an expression of regret or apology.

patterns.name: Parliamentary procedure, policy, and formal argumentation
patterns.context: Formal statements about parliamentary procedure, proposals, policy, or international affairs; strong activations often fall on Spanish articles or German transitions, but their positions are not fully consistent.
patterns.domain: European Parliament debates, Spanish, German, Portuguese

patterns.name: Question titles and opening questions on Q&A sites
patterns.context: A question title is followed by the author introducing themselves as a beginner, describing the background, and asking several questions; the peak falls on «so».

patterns.name: Apology and explanation of being busy in email
patterns.context: An email reply explains the reason for a delayed response, says the sender is currently busy, and promises to get in touch later.

8_962.concept: 正式话语中的陈述与转接
8_962.description: 主要出现在欧洲议会正式发言中，涉及发言者表态、程序或政策论述；另见问答开场及邮件道歉。强激活位置跨语言、跨句法位置，难归于单一词形。

patterns.name: 议会发言中转入第一人称陈述
patterns.trigger: «ich»7« be»1«gr»1«üße»4« es»1« da»3«her»2；«ich»7« habe»6« die»1 Stimmerklärun；«Me»4iner Meinung« nach；«Me»3ines Eracht«ens；«W»7«ie»5« Sie»6« w«4«issen»4
patterns.context: 多处激活出现在议会发言里，尤其是句首或新段开始的发言者立场、评价、解释或对听众讲话；[1] 还在句中出现「ich」及相关词。
patterns.domain: 欧洲议会正式辩论，德语为主

patterns.name: 正式议会发言中的感谢与致歉
patterns.context: 在意大利语发言中，感谢议会的贡献后转入遗憾或致歉表达。
patterns.domain: 欧洲议会正式发言，意大利语

patterns.name: 议会程序、政策与正式论证
patterns.trigger: «Se»3ñora President«a»2；«el Protocolo»；«Los mercados de la aviación»；«das Thema»；«der Vorschlag der Kommission»；«Europäische Sicherheitsstrategie»；«Ir»ão
patterns.context: 围绕议会程序、提案、政策或国际事务作正式陈述；强激活常落在西语冠词或德语发言转折处，但触发位置并不完全一致。
patterns.domain: 欧洲议会辩论，西班牙语、德语、葡萄牙语

patterns.name: 问答网站问题标题与提问开场
patterns.trigger: «Q«:»1；«Questions on DHCP server setup»；«I»5«'m»2 fairly new to networking of this «so»10« I»6« have»2 a lot of questions
patterns.context: 先给出问题标题，再以新手身份说明背景并提出多个问题；峰值落在「so」。

patterns.name: 邮件中的道歉与忙碌说明
patterns.trigger: «Sorry»1« that»3« i»2 didn't respond；«I»6« am»4 super busy right now «but»9
patterns.context: 邮件回复中解释未及时回复的原因，并说明当前很忙、之后会联系。

en.description: All passages activate near sentence boundaries, line breaks, or intra-sentence linking structures, but the following tokens and semantics vary widely; these samples alone do not establish a more specific, stable trigger.

patterns.name: Sentence boundary/following text after sentence-final punctuation
patterns.context: An existing sentence ends with a period or question mark, and activation falls near the line break and the start of the next sentence or paragraph; however, the specific words after the boundary vary greatly across examples
patterns.domain: Parliamentary speeches, Q&A, encyclopedias, emails, forums, and web text

patterns.name: Following expression introduced by an intra-sentence cause or result
patterns.context: The preceding text states background, a reason, or a process, then introduces a result, evaluation, or follow-up explanation; however, «so» is also merely an ordinary connective in several sentences
patterns.domain: General narratives, parliamentary argumentation, forum questions, and product descriptions

patterns.name: Near emphatic or summarizing predicates
patterns.context: Activation falls near predicates, interrogative words, or subordinate structures in German or English sentences, without a stable shared syntactic position or semantic role
patterns.domain: Parliamentary speeches, encyclopedias, forums, and web descriptions

patterns.name: Greetings and thanks in email
patterns.context: Near the beginning of an email body or a polite expression; email samples also contain ordinary text following sentence boundaries, so greetings or thanks cannot be confirmed as stable triggers

8_962.description: 所有片段都在句界、换行或句中连接结构附近激活，但后续 token 与语义差异很大；仅凭这些样本难以确定更具体、稳定的触发条件。

patterns.name: 句末标点后的句界/后续文本
patterns.trigger: 句号后的 «↵»、«W»、«Me»、«Die»、«V»、«I»、«They»、«Hello» 等句首 token；第2段另有 «?» 后的换行
patterns.context: 已有句子以句号或问号结束，激活落在换行及下一句或下一段的开头附近；但不同例子中句界后的具体词差异很大
patterns.domain: 议会发言、问答、百科、邮件、论坛及网页文字

patterns.name: 句中因果或结果引出的后续表达
patterns.trigger: «so»，以及「Wettbewerb kon«n»3«te»4« sich entfalten, insbesondere im Bereich der Flugpreise,« was»8 Vorteile … br«acht»2«e»5«.»10」中的 «was»
patterns.context: 前文陈述背景、原因或过程，随后引出结果、评价或后续说明；但 «so» 在多个句子中也只是普通连接词
patterns.domain: 一般叙述、议会论述、论坛提问及产品描述

patterns.name: 强调或总结性谓语附近
patterns.trigger: «hat»、«soll»、«warum»、«nach»、«it» 等；分别见 «hat» die Kommission、«soll»te、war«um»、«so» it seemed、«that» they
patterns.context: 激活落在德语或英语句子中谓语、疑问词或从属结构附近，缺乏稳定的共同句法位置或语义角色
patterns.domain: 议会发言、百科、论坛及网页描述

patterns.name: 邮件中的问候与致谢
patterns.trigger: «Hello»、«Thank» you very much；以及句界附近的 «I»
patterns.context: 邮件正文的开头或礼貌表达附近；邮件样本还包含普通的句界后续文本，无法确认问候或致谢本身是稳定触发条件

en.concept: Parliamentary speech boundaries and polite interaction
en.description: Activations occur in multilingual European Parliament transcripts, especially around chair titles, direct responses, polite first-person stances, and sentence/paragraph boundaries. There are also scattered subword fragments and several specific policy topics, with no confirmed shared trigger mechanism.

patterns.name: Parliamentary chair/member titles
patterns.context: Addressing the chair, naming a member, or directly responding to a member in parliamentary speech, commonly at the sentence opening or after a line break
patterns.domain: European Parliament oral debates and minutes

patterns.name: Polite responses and stance expression in parliamentary speech
patterns.context: First-person statements, thanks, agreement, or an introduction of a personal view, often adjacent to direct address to a member

patterns.name: Sentence-final punctuation and subsequent speech boundaries
patterns.context: Marks the end of a sentence, a change of speaker, or a new paragraph; activation often falls on punctuation, a following connector, or a sentence-initial word

patterns.name: Subword fragments within German words
patterns.context: Complex German words or words are split into multiple tokens; it is unclear whether activation is triggered by a specific word form, subword boundary, or nearby syntax

patterns.name: Subword fragments within Portuguese words
patterns.context: Portuguese words are split into subwords, occurring in contexts of statements, thanks, or event reporting

patterns.name: Subword fragments within Spanish words
patterns.context: Spanish words are split into multiple tokens, involving past tense, conditional, or verb inflection

patterns.name: Policy arguments and contrastive connectors
patterns.context: Connects arguments, supplementary explanations, or contrasts in continuous policy statements; trigger tokens are scattered, with no stable single lexical item

patterns.name: Voting procedures and roll-call records
patterns.context: Describes whether a member is on the list, participates in a vote, or how their vote is handled

patterns.name: Airline markets and competition
patterns.context: Discusses competition in the airline market and its effects on consumers

patterns.name: International agreements and market access
patterns.context: Discusses agreements related to Canada, restrictions, and market access

patterns.name: Media pluralism
patterns.context: Raises media pluralism as a topic or argument

patterns.name: Regional price/industry changes
patterns.context: Narrates increases across different industries or regions

patterns.name: Topic fragments that do not fit a stable pattern
patterns.context: Content concerns the Macedonia report, oral questions, nuclear issues, and complacency and follow-up work; a shared trigger is unclear

8_962.concept: 议会发言边界与礼貌互动
8_962.description: 激活出现在多语种欧洲议会逐字记录中，尤其是主席称谓、直接回应、第一人称礼貌立场表达及句末/段落边界；另有分散的子词片段与若干特定政策议题，无法确认是否共享触发机制。

patterns.name: 议会主席/议员称谓
patterns.context: 议会发言中的主席称呼、点名或直接回应议员，常见于句首/换行后
patterns.domain: 欧洲议会口头辩论及会议记录

patterns.name: 议会发言中的礼貌回应与立场表达
patterns.trigger: «ich»« habe»；«Mein»；«begrüße»；«gostaria»；«Me»« encantaría»；«estoy»« completamente de acuerdo»；«es»« evidente»
patterns.context: 第一人称陈述、感谢、赞同或引出个人观点，常与直接对议员讲话相邻

patterns.name: 句末标点及其后的发言边界
patterns.context: 标记句子结束、发言转换或新段落；激活常落在标点、紧随其后的连接词或句首词上

patterns.name: 德语词内子词片段
patterns.context: 德语形态复杂词或词被分成多个 token；无法确定激活是由具体词形、子词边界还是邻近句法触发

patterns.name: 葡萄牙语词内子词片段
patterns.context: 葡萄牙语词被拆分成子词，出现于陈述、感谢或记录事件的语境

patterns.name: 西班牙语词内子词片段
patterns.context: 西班牙语词被切分为多个 token，涉及过去时、条件式或动词变位

patterns.name: 政策论述及转折连接语
patterns.context: 连接论据、补充说明或转折，出现在连续的政策陈述中；触发 token 分散，未见稳定单一词项

patterns.name: 投票程序及点名记录
patterns.trigger: «Stimmerklärun»；«nicht auf der Liste»；«nicht»；«an der Abstimmung teilnehmen»；«tomado en cuenta»
patterns.context: 说明议员是否列入名单、参与投票或其投票情况如何处理

patterns.name: 航空市场与竞争
patterns.context: 讨论航空市场竞争及其对消费者的影响

patterns.name: 国际协议与市场准入
patterns.context: 讨论与加拿大相关的协议、限制及市场准入

patterns.name: 媒体多元主义
patterns.context: 提出媒体多元主义作为议题或论点

patterns.name: 区域价格/应用行业变化
patterns.trigger: «os aumentos variaram»；«sector de aplicação»；«Registou-se um aumento»
patterns.context: 叙述不同应用行业或区域中出现的增幅
patterns.domain: 葡萄牙语政策或经济陈述

patterns.name: 未能归入稳定模式的议题片段
patterns.context: 内容分别涉及马其顿报告、口头质询、核问题及自满与后续工作；共同触发因素不明确

en.description: All passages come from multilingual European Parliament debates; activation most consistently falls on periods and nearby line breaks or sentence-initial positions. Sporadic connectives, parliamentary forms of address, and varied policy vocabulary also appear, without a unified semantic theme.

patterns.name: Sentence-final period
patterns.context: Activation often appears on the period ending a complete sentence; a line break or new sentence sometimes follows.
patterns.domain: Multilingual formal speeches in European Parliament debate records

patterns.name: Parliamentary line breaks and speaker-turn formatting
patterns.context: A line break, president’s or member’s form of address, or other transcript formatting follows a period; activation falls on the line break or an adjacent marker.

patterns.name: New sentence or subsequent argument after a sentence ending
patterns.context: A new sentence or paragraph begins after a complete statement; activation is scattered across sentence-initial subword fragments, with no stable lexical or grammatical category apparent.

patterns.name: Contrastive or causal links in argumentation
patterns.context: Appears when linking reasons, results, or supplementary content, but the trigger words and positions vary by language, and most connectives are unmarked.
patterns.domain: Spanish, German, and Portuguese parliamentary speeches

patterns.name: Parliamentary procedure and forms of address
patterns.context: Occasional activations when addressing the president, commissioners, or members, and when referring to speeches, votes, or lists.

patterns.name: Substantive policy vocabulary
patterns.context: Topics include competition, Palestinian funding, media pluralism, fair trial, nuclear issues, or mental health; there is no shared pattern of specific topic words.

8_962.concept: 议会转录中的句界标记
8_962.description: 各段均来自多语言欧洲议会辩论；激活最稳定地落在句号及邻近的换行、句首位置，另有零散连接词、议会称谓和不同政策词汇，缺少统一语义主题。

patterns.name: 句末句号
patterns.context: 激活常出现在完整句子的句号上；句号后有时接换行或新句。
patterns.domain: 欧洲议会辩论记录，多语言正式发言

patterns.name: 议会换行与发言轮次格式
patterns.context: 句号后出现换行、主席或议员称谓等记录格式；激活落在换行或邻近标记上。

patterns.name: 句末后转入新句或后续论述
patterns.context: 完整陈述结束后开启新句或新段，激活分散在句首词片段；未见稳定的词义或语法类别。

patterns.name: 论述转折或因果连接
patterns.context: 连接理由、结果或补充内容时出现，但触发词语言与位置不一致，且多数连接词并未标记。
patterns.domain: 西班牙语、德语、葡萄牙语议会发言

patterns.name: 议会程序及称谓
patterns.context: 称呼主席、委员或议员，以及提及发言、表决和名单等程序时偶有激活。

patterns.name: 实质政策议题词汇
patterns.context: 涉及竞争、巴勒斯坦融资、媒体多元、公正审判、核问题或心理健康等议题；没有共同的特定主题词模式。

en.description: Responds mainly to formal multilingual European Parliament speeches and procedural records, including forms of address, speaker transitions, policy issues, and voting explanations; it also activates on a Portuguese programming comparison and a Spanish Ubuntu support question in two non-parliamentary technical Q&A passages.

patterns.name: Parliamentary forms of address and procedural language
patterns.context: Forms of address for the president, commissioners, or members, and procedural statements in European Parliament speeches or records; includes speech openings, voting, explanations of votes, and apologies

patterns.name: Transitions and positions in parliamentary speeches
patterns.context: Connecting arguments, expressing thanks or agreement, proposing continued dialogue, or adding information in formal speeches; usually in a member’s direct speech rather than purely in titles or agenda text

patterns.name: Policy issues and public affairs argumentation
patterns.context: Statements about policy issues such as broadcasting, airline competition, public health, or nuclear issues; specific topics vary, but all are in a parliamentary policy-discussion context
patterns.domain: EuroParl, policy debates and committee topics

patterns.name: Voting constraints and absence explanations
patterns.context: Procedural contexts referring to being unable to vote, a member not appearing on a list, or records/explanations concluding a vote

patterns.name: Spanish-language conversational technical Q&A
patterns.context: A user asks a question in Spanish and describes Ubuntu live CD and Windows failures; unlike formal parliamentary text

patterns.name: Portuguese technical comparison Q&A
patterns.context: Compares whether software validation occurs inside a Controller method or before calling it, then asks which approach is more valuable

8_962.concept: 多语种对话与议事文本
8_962.description: 主要响应多语种欧洲议会正式发言及程序记录，包含称呼、发言承接、政策议题和投票说明；另对两段非议会技术问答中的葡语编程比较与西语 Ubuntu 求助有激活。

patterns.name: 议会称呼与程序话语
patterns.context: 欧洲议会发言或会议记录中，主席、委员或议员的称呼及发言程序语句；包括发言开头、投票、解释投票和致歉等场景

patterns.name: 议会发言中的承接与表态
patterns.context: 正式发言中连接论述、表达感谢或赞同、提出继续对话与补充信息；常处于议员直接发言，而非纯标题或议程文字

patterns.name: 政策议题与公共事务论述
patterns.context: 涉及广播、航空竞争、公共健康或核问题等政策议题的陈述；具体主题各异，但均处于议会政策讨论语境
patterns.domain: EuroParl，政策辩论与委员会议题

patterns.name: 投票受限及缺席说明
patterns.trigger: «não poderem participar na votação», «tomado em conta», «não estava na lista», «Stimmerklärungen»
patterns.context: 提及未能参加投票、议员不在名单上，或记录／结束投票解释的程序语境

patterns.name: 西班牙语口语技术问答
patterns.trigger: «y cual es el problema?»；«estoy usando un cd-live de ubuntu»
patterns.context: 用户以西班牙语询问问题并说明 Ubuntu live CD 和 Windows 故障；不像正式议会文本

patterns.name: 葡语技术比较问答
patterns.context: 比较软件验证发生在 Controller 方法内部还是调用前，并追问哪种方式更有价值

en.description: Activations are scattered across subword fragments within words in multilingual text, with occasional sentence-final punctuation, line breaks, and common connectives; the instances lack stable semantics or a reliable single trigger.

patterns.name: Completing word forms within sentences
patterns.context: Markers often fall on word-initial or intra-word subword fragments in continuous natural-language sentences; no unified meaning or part of speech can be confirmed, and other passages also split words without being marked
patterns.domain: German, Spanish, and Portuguese parliamentary corpora and Spanish Q&A

patterns.name: Sentence-final punctuation and line breaks
patterns.context: Appears at sentence endings, paragraph boundaries, or speaker changes; repeated in several EuroParl passages, but punctuation is not a stable trigger

patterns.name: Clause after Portuguese “porque”
patterns.context: Appears when explaining a reason or introducing a following clause; however, the same word may simply be a common connective in the corpus, and evidence is insufficient to establish an independent role

patterns.name: Ubuntu version-number fragment
patterns.context: Adjacent to digits in an Ubuntu version number, in a technical failure description in an IRC conversation; a single occurrence

patterns.name: Spanish “ya que” and beginner help request
patterns.context: Appears in the help-seeking context “¿Alguien me podría ayudar… ya que soy nuevo…”; no clear link to other high-activation passages is apparent

8_962.description: 激活散布于多语种文本的词内子词片段，偶见句末标点、换行及常见连接词；各处缺乏稳定语义或可靠的单一触发条件。

patterns.name: 句中补全词形
patterns.trigger: 词内部被拆分标记的 token，如德语 « w»achsenden、« m»üssen、« soll»te、« Me»iner，西语 « incl»u»ían、« ofrec»ían、« t»ien»es，葡语 « pod»erem、« alg»uns、« est»ão、« deb»at»emos
patterns.context: 标记常落在词首或词内的子词片段，周围是连续的自然语言句子；没有可确认的统一词义或词性，且其他片段同样会拆词但未标记
patterns.domain: 德语、西班牙语、葡萄牙语的议会语料及西语问答

patterns.name: 句末标点与换行
patterns.context: 出现在句子结束、段落或发言切换处；在 EuroParl 多段中重复，但标点并非稳定触发条件

patterns.name: 葡语“porque”后的从句
patterns.context: 解释原因或引出后续从句时出现；但同词也可能只是语料中常见连接词，证据不足以确定其独立作用

patterns.name: Ubuntu 版本号片段
patterns.context: 紧邻 Ubuntu 版本号数字，属于 IRC 对话中的技术故障描述；单次出现

patterns.name: 西语“ya que”与新手求助
patterns.context: 出现在“¿Alguien me podría ayudar… ya que soy nuevo…”的求助语境；与其他片段的高激活未显示明确关联

en.description: Activations are distributed across multilingual text and commonly occur at sentence boundaries, clause introducers, and subwords split from words; there are also parliamentary forms of address, stance expressions, and sporadic morphological fragments, with no single semantic theme.

patterns.name: “que” after a sentence ending and the following clause
patterns.context: Occurs near the middle or end of a sentence, followed by a declarative, causal, purposive, or supplementary clause; typically in continuation contexts after a comma or period.
patterns.domain: Multilingual political speeches, parliamentary debates, and Spanish academic writing

patterns.name: Inter-sentence cohesion in German parliamentary speeches
patterns.context: At a transition between sentences or clause introduction in a parliamentary speech; nearby highlighted words often include periods, line breaks, and first-person or audience-directed expressions.

patterns.name: Sentence-final punctuation and line-break boundaries
patterns.context: A period is followed by a line break or a new sentence; punctuation activation is clear, but not all punctuation boundaries trigger it.
patterns.domain: European Parliament records and dialogue text

patterns.name: Portuguese conjunctions and verb-morphology fragments
patterns.context: In Portuguese sentences, activation occurs on contrastive conjunctions, verb endings, or participial forms; semantic and syntactic positions are inconsistent.
patterns.domain: StackExchange Portuguese Q&A and Portuguese European Parliament speeches

patterns.name: Subword fragments within Spanish words
patterns.context: Spanish words are split into subword tokens, with activation on the stem or suffix; surrounding content includes oral speeches, political commentary, and academic philosophy texts.
patterns.domain: Spanish parliamentary speeches and academic texts

patterns.name: Parliamentary polite address or speech markers
patterns.context: Parliamentary speech includes an address to the chair, a form of address for a member, or a reference to a committee.

patterns.name: Expressions of personal stance and evaluation
patterns.context: Speakers express welcome, evaluation, or condemnation, followed by a judgment about an event or action.

patterns.name: Other isolated word fragments
patterns.context: Local subword activations within words do not show a stable shared syntactic or semantic condition; paragraph 1 in particular is from a technical Q&A, while the rest are parliamentary contexts.
patterns.domain: StackExchange technical Q&A and European Parliament speeches

8_962.concept: 句际衔接与多语种子词
8_962.description: 激活分布于多语种文本，常见于句际边界、从句引入词及被拆分的词内子词；另有议会称呼、立场表达和零散形态片段，未见单一语义主题。

patterns.name: 句末后的“que”及后续从句
patterns.context: 出现在句中或句末附近，后接陈述、因果、目的或补充说明从句；通常处于逗号或句号之后的延续语境。
patterns.domain: 多语种政治演讲、议会辩论及西班牙语学术论述

patterns.name: 德语议会发言中的句际衔接
patterns.context: 议会演讲的句际过渡或从句引入位置；高亮词附近常有句号、换行及第一人称或面向听众的表达。

patterns.name: 句末标点与换行边界
patterns.context: 句号后接换行或新句；标点激活明显，但并非所有标点边界都会触发。
patterns.domain: 欧洲议会记录及对话文本

patterns.name: 葡语连词与动词形态片段
patterns.context: 葡语句中，转折连词、动词词尾或分词形态处出现激活；语义与句法位置不统一。
patterns.domain: StackExchange 葡语问答、葡语欧洲议会发言

patterns.name: 西语词内子词片段
patterns.context: 西语词被拆分为子词 token，激活落在词干或词尾；周边内容包括口语发言、政治评论和哲学学术文本。
patterns.domain: 西语议会发言与学术文本

patterns.name: 议会礼貌称呼或发言标记
patterns.context: 议会发言中出现主席称呼、对议员的称谓或委员会相关表达。

patterns.name: 人物立场与评价表达
patterns.trigger: « be»2«gr»2ü«ße»3 es；« Consider»3«o»5 verdadeiramente escandaloso；« me»1 parece inadequad
patterns.context: 发言者表达欢迎、评价或谴责，后接对事件或行为的判断。

patterns.name: 其他孤立词片段
patterns.context: 局部词内子词激活，未显示稳定的共同句法或语义条件；尤其第1段来自技术问答，其余为议会语境。
patterns.domain: StackExchange 技术问答与欧洲议会发言

en.description: Activations commonly occur on sentence-final punctuation and line breaks, and also on viewpoints, contrasts, causal expressions, or modal expressions at the start of new sentences; speaker-turn changes and truncated continuation sentences in parliamentary speeches also activate. Patterns vary across languages and styles and are not fully consistent.

patterns.name: Sentence-final punctuation and paragraph boundaries
patterns.context: At the end of a sentence or speech, followed by a line break or the start of a new sentence/speech
patterns.domain: Multilingual written text, parliamentary speeches, forums, and technical text

patterns.name: Causal or explanatory connectives
patterns.context: Linking a reason, explanation, or following clause; some occur within sentences in the passages

patterns.name: Viewpoint, contrast, and modality expressions
patterns.context: Introducing a viewpoint, contrast, judgment, or obligation
patterns.domain: German parliamentary text, Portuguese forum text

patterns.name: Speaker turns and forms of address
patterns.context: Speaker attribution, forms of address, or turn changes in parliamentary speeches

patterns.name: Unfinished continuation
patterns.context: Further explanation continues after the sentence ending, or the sentence remains unfinished at the excerpt boundary

8_962.description: 激活常见于句末标点和换行，也见于新句的观点、转折、因果或情态表达；议会发言轮次切换及截断后续句也有激活。跨语言、跨文体，模式不完全统一。

patterns.name: 句末标点与段落边界
patterns.context: 句子或发言结束、随后换行或进入新句/发言处
patterns.domain: 多语种书面文本、议会发言、论坛与技术文本

patterns.name: 因果或解释性连接词
patterns.context: 连接原因、解释或后续从句；在片段中部分出现在句中
patterns.domain: 葡萄牙语、英语夹杂的 IRC 对话

patterns.name: 观点、转折及情态表达
patterns.context: 引出观点、转折、判断或义务表达
patterns.domain: 德语议会文本、葡萄牙语论坛文本

patterns.name: 发言轮次与称呼
patterns.context: 议会发言中发言者署名、称呼或轮次切换

patterns.name: 未完结的后续表达
patterns.trigger: 「Wer daran arbeiten möchte」「será conveniente」「apesar da longevidade」
patterns.context: 句末之后继续展开说明，或句子在截取处仍未结束

en.description: Activations are scattered across sentence-final punctuation, turn-taking, common connectives, and first-person speech in multilingual dialogue; parliamentary records are most common, with technical Q&A and help requests also present. No single stable word meaning or domain-specific feature is apparent.

patterns.name: Sentence-final punctuation and following discourse transition
patterns.context: Commonly appears after a sentence closes, immediately before a new paragraph, speaker name, or turn; periods themselves also show strong activation in several passages.
patterns.domain: Parliamentary records, forum Q&A, and IRC conversations

patterns.name: German causal and subordinate-clause connectives
patterns.context: Connect subordinate clauses or coordinated content within German sentences, or introduce a conclusion; «und» in particular occurs in contexts such as committee responses and statements of opinion.

patterns.name: Portuguese subjective statements and contrast
patterns.context: Expressing difficulty, judgment, or contrast in first-person speech; «que» occurs in statements or explanatory subordinate clauses.

patterns.name: Swedish parliamentary question words
patterns.context: When members or the president speak, ask questions, or respond in the first person; these words occur respectively at sentence openings, in auxiliary constructions, and in subordinate clauses.

patterns.name: German parliamentary forms of address and speech format
patterns.context: Near parliamentary forms of address to the president and member turn-taking; activation is distributed across titles, greetings, and speech transitions.

patterns.name: Dutch forms of address to the president and speaker transitions
patterns.context: When a member addresses the president or explains why they have requested the floor.

patterns.name: Spanish greetings and thanks
patterns.context: When a user opens with a greeting, explains a request, and expresses thanks.

patterns.name: Portuguese technical log discussion
patterns.context: Discussing logging attack-related information and expressing an assessment or security concern.

patterns.name: European parliamentary procedural language
patterns.context: Appears in fixed parliamentary discourse about meeting procedures, question scheduling, or thanks.

8_962.description: 激活分散于多语种对话中的句末标点、话轮交接、常见连接词及第一人称发言；议会记录最常见，另见技术问答和求助，未显示单一稳定的词义或领域特征。

patterns.name: 句末标点与后续话语连接
patterns.trigger: 句号后的 «↵»、引号或话轮/发言人标记；以及句号前后的 «.»
patterns.context: 常见于一句话收束后紧接新段、发言人姓名或新说话轮次；多个段落中句号本身也有较强激活。
patterns.domain: 议会记录、论坛问答与 IRC 对话

patterns.name: 德语因果与从句连接词
patterns.context: 德语句中连接从句、并列内容或引出结论时；尤其 «und» 出现在委员会答复、观点陈述等语境。

patterns.name: 葡萄牙语主观陈述与转折
patterns.context: 第一人称发言中表达困难、判断或转折；«que» 出现在陈述或解释性从句里。

patterns.name: 瑞典语议会问答词
patterns.context: 议员或主席以第一人称发言、提问或回应时；这些词分别出现在句首、助动结构和从句中。

patterns.name: 德语议会称呼与发言格式
patterns.context: 议会主席称呼和议员发言交接附近；激活分布在称谓、问候和发言连接处。

patterns.name: 荷兰语主席称呼及发言交接
patterns.context: 议员向主席发言、解释为何请求发言时。
patterns.domain: 欧洲议会荷兰语会议记录

patterns.name: 西班牙语问候与感谢
patterns.context: 用户以问候开场并说明请求、表达感谢时。

patterns.name: 葡萄牙语技术日志讨论
patterns.context: 讨论把攻击相关信息写入日志，并表达判断及安全性疑问。

patterns.name: 欧洲议会程序性用语
patterns.trigger: «keine Aussprache»、«Jag har ungefär 100 frågor»、«Tack för dina välkomnande ord»
patterns.context: 会议程序、提问安排或致谢等固定议会话语中出现。

en.description: Activations occur mainly on connectives, syntactic function words, contrast markers, and parliamentary speech transitions in multilingual discourse, and are also scattered across punctuation, formatting boundaries, and proper nouns; not all instances can be explained by the same trigger.

patterns.name: Spanish and Portuguese que clause connectors
patterns.context: Introduce explanatory, supplementary, or subordinate-clause content in Spanish or Portuguese parliamentary/forum text; [1] is “Hay que tener en cuenta que…”, [4] is “sabe que…”, and [3] is “porque algunos diputados…”
patterns.domain: Spanish forum text and European Parliament speeches

patterns.name: Portuguese contrast marker
patterns.context: A sentence-initial contrastive adverb in Portuguese technical Q&A introduces a situation that is contrary to or limited relative to the preceding proposal

patterns.name: German parliamentary connectives and syntactic words
patterns.context: Inter-sentence transitions, predicates, and interrogative/relative structures in German explanations or parliamentary discourse; local grammatical functions vary
patterns.domain: European Parliament texts and German software documentation

patterns.name: Transitions and evaluative expressions in parliamentary speeches
patterns.context: Members continue a previous point, express an evaluation, or state a subsequent judgment; no single fixed trigger word is apparent

patterns.name: Punctuation and formatting boundaries
patterns.context: Positive activations occur near sentence endings, line breaks, headings, or forms of address in parliamentary speeches; exact positions and functions vary
patterns.domain: Forum text, parliamentary transcripts, and headings

patterns.name: Unexplained proper nouns and local word fragments
patterns.context: Activation falls on forms of address, proper nouns, or local word fragments; isolated instances do not establish stable contextual conditions
patterns.domain: Forum text and European Parliament speeches

8_962.description: 激活多见于多语种语篇中的连接词、句法功能词、转折标记及议会发言承接语，也散见于标点、版式边界和专名；各实例并非都能由同一触发条件解释。

patterns.name: 西伊语 que 从句连接词
patterns.context: 在西班牙语或葡萄牙语议会/论坛文本中，引出解释、补充或从句内容；[1]为“Hay que tener en cuenta que…”，[4]为“sabe que…”，[3]为“porque algunos diputados…”
patterns.domain: 西班牙语论坛文本及欧洲议会发言

patterns.name: 葡语转折标记
patterns.context: 葡萄牙语技术问答中，句首用转折副词引出与前述方案相反或受限的情况

patterns.name: 德语议会连接与句法词
patterns.context: 德语说明或议会语篇中的句间衔接、谓语及疑问/关系结构；各处局部语法功能不同
patterns.domain: 欧洲议会文本及德语软件说明

patterns.name: 议会发言中的承接与评价表达
patterns.trigger: « Me»4«in»（“Mein Ausschuss”）、« be»2«grü»ße»4；« Dev»5«o»2；« e»5« pens»3«o»5；« será»1
patterns.context: 议员发言中承接前文、表达评价或陈述后续判断；未见单一固定触发词
patterns.domain: 多语种欧洲议会口语转录

patterns.name: 标点及版式边界
patterns.context: 议会发言的句末、换行、标题或称呼等转录边界附近出现正激活，具体位置和功能不完全一致
patterns.domain: 论坛文本、议会转录及标题

patterns.name: 未解释的专名及局部词片
patterns.trigger: « Jorge»2；« running»相关片段；«I»3«vo»及人名片段
patterns.context: 激活落在称呼、专名或局部切分词片上，无法从这些孤立实例确定稳定的上下文条件
patterns.domain: 论坛文本及欧洲议会发言

en.concept: Sentence-boundary markers and continuation after sentences
en.description: All paragraphs share the period as a sentence-boundary marker, often introducing a new sentence; some paragraphs also activate line breaks and sentence-initial transitions, parliamentary forms of address, or narrative expressions. Languages and topics differ substantially, while other word-fragment patterns are more local.

patterns.name: Period at sentence end or within a sentence
patterns.context: A period ends a declarative sentence, often followed by a sentence-initial contrastive word or a new sentence; the trigger is the punctuation itself and is not limited to paragraph-final positions
patterns.domain: Multilingual text, including papers and parliamentary speeches

patterns.name: Line break after a period
patterns.context: A line break follows a period, often introducing a new speaker or turn in parliamentary speech
patterns.domain: Parliamentary records; paragraph 1 also contains a line break in technical Q&A text

patterns.name: Sentence-initial contrast or continuation words
patterns.context: After a period or paragraph boundary, a new sentence begins with a contrastive, continuative, or discourse-progressing word; the specific words differ across examples

patterns.name: Spanish forms of address and polite expressions
patterns.context: In parliamentary speech, directly addresses another person or explains an action the speaker previously took

patterns.name: Addressing the chair in German
patterns.context: After a line break, names the chair and opens with a polite greeting

patterns.name: Italian emphasis or contrastive transitions
patterns.context: In a parliamentary sentence, introduces a contrast with “but” or uses “I must” to introduce a reminder

patterns.name: Portuguese evaluation and inference expressions
patterns.context: Evaluates project management performance and introduces a judgment with “it can be said”

patterns.name: German plural past-tense verbs
patterns.context: Describes attendance and decisions in parliamentary speech; activation falls on split word fragments

8_962.description: 各段共同出现句号这一句界标记，且句号常引出新句；部分段落还激活换行及句首衔接、议会称呼或叙述用语。多语种与主题差异显著，其他词片段模式较局部。

patterns.name: 句末或句中句号
patterns.context: 句号结束一个陈述句，常紧接句首转折词或新句；触发的是标点本身，不限于句末段落
patterns.domain: 多语种文本，包括论文和议会发言

patterns.name: 句号后换行
patterns.context: 句号后出现换行，常在议会发言中引入新的发言者或话轮
patterns.domain: 议会记录；第1段亦有技术问答文本中的换行

patterns.name: 句首转折或承接词
patterns.context: 句号或段落边界后出现新句的转折、承接或论述推进词；各处具体词汇不同
patterns.domain: 葡语问答、英语数学论文

patterns.name: 西语说话者称呼及礼貌表达
patterns.context: 议会发言中直接向他人表达或说明发言者曾采取的行动

patterns.name: 德语称呼主席
patterns.context: 换行后点名主席并以礼貌问候开场

patterns.name: 意大利语强调或转折衔接
patterns.context: 议会句中以“但是”转折，或以“我必须”引出提醒

patterns.name: 葡语评价及推断表达
patterns.context: 评价项目管理表现，并引出“可以说”的判断

patterns.name: 德语复数过去式动词
patterns.context: 议会发言中叙述出席情况及作出决定，激活标记落在被拆分的词片段上

en.concept: Sentence and paragraph transitions and discourse markers
en.description: Activations often fall on periods, line breaks, and transitions to new sentences, and also appear on contrastive, inferential, negative, or limiting expressions; Portuguese, Dutch, and German intra-word fragments also occur, without stable semantic conditions.

patterns.name: Sentence-final period and sentence-initial text after a line break
patterns.context: Near paragraph boundaries or the start of a new sentence, with activations falling on a period, line break, or immediately adjacent position across several examples; no particular topic is required.

patterns.name: Contrastive or explanatory connectives
patterns.context: Linking clauses, especially when introducing supplementary, contrastive, or inferential content; several activations also fall on adjacent punctuation.
patterns.domain: General argumentation, academic writing, forum text

patterns.name: Limiting or evaluative expressions
patterns.context: Expressing negation, limitation, or an evaluation of an approach; some examples are adjacent to sentence-final punctuation.

patterns.name: Sentence/paragraph boundaries in European Parliament text
patterns.context: Sentence endings or paragraph breaks in German or Dutch parliamentary speeches, with activation falling specifically on punctuation or boundary tokens.

patterns.name: Portuguese intra-word fragments
patterns.context: Words are split into multiple tokens in Portuguese text; activation is distributed across intra-word fragments and surrounding punctuation, with no clear unified semantic condition.

patterns.name: Intra-sentence transitions in code Q&A
patterns.context: After a code snippet, the text shifts to a first-person explanation commenting on a prior assumption or documentation.

patterns.name: Argumentation following an equation
patterns.context: After a mathematical equation or technical statement ends, the text continues by explaining its significance or limiting the subsequent discussion.

patterns.name: Local word fragments that do not fit a clear pattern
patterns.context: These activations occur within or near ordinary words in Dutch and German text; the available context does not support a more specific shared trigger.

8_962.description: 激活多落在句号、换行和新句衔接处，也见于转折、推论、否定或限制表达；另有葡语、荷兰语和德语词内片段，未显示稳定语义条件。

patterns.name: 句末句号与换行后的句首
patterns.trigger: 句号 «.» 后接换行；随后常出现 «↵» 或句首 «I»、«We»
patterns.context: 段落边界或新句开头附近，多个示例中激活落在句号、换行或其后紧邻位置；不要求特定主题。
patterns.domain: 跨领域散文、论坛文本、论文

patterns.name: 转折或解释衔接词
patterns.trigger: « and»、« however»、« Therefore»、« but» 等连接成分
patterns.context: 连接前后分句，尤其引入补充、转折或推论时；若干激活也落在相邻标点上。
patterns.domain: 一般论述、学术写作、论坛文本

patterns.name: 限制或判断性表达
patterns.trigger: « but»、« doesn't seem to»、« no sense»、« not generally possible»
patterns.context: 表达否定、限制或对做法作判断；部分例子紧邻句末标点。

patterns.name: 欧盟议会文本中的句末/段落边界
patterns.trigger: «.»、«↵»，如“der Antwort der Kommissarin erhalten”后的标点
patterns.context: 德语或荷兰语议会发言的句末或换段位置，激活具体落在标点或边界 token 上。

patterns.name: 葡萄牙语词内片段
patterns.context: 葡语文本中词语被分成多个 token；激活分布在词内片段及周边标点，未见清楚统一的语义条件。
patterns.domain: StackExchange 葡萄牙语技术问答

patterns.name: 代码问答中的句内衔接
patterns.context: 代码片段后转入第一人称说明，对先前假设或文档作评论。

patterns.name: 公式后承接论述
patterns.context: 数学公式或技术陈述结束后，继续解释其意义或限定后续讨论。

patterns.name: 无法归入明确模式的局部词片段
patterns.trigger: « zijn»、« uitge»（所在词被截断）、« Me»、« hat»、« bere»、«begrü»
patterns.context: 这些激活出现在荷兰语、德语文本的普通词语内部或附近，现有上下文不足以支持更具体的共同触发条件。

en.description: Activations are distributed across sentence boundaries, paragraph boundaries, and points where an argument progresses, often accompanied by contrastive, additive, or explanatory function words. They also cover text adjacent to mathematical formulas, Spanish political speeches, and forum questions, with no single stable word or theme.

patterns.name: Sentence-initial contrastive or additive connectors
patterns.context: Connects preceding text to the following argument, often near a comma or period; examples occur in both English and Spanish

patterns.name: Discourse progression after sentence boundaries
patterns.context: Introduces the next explanation, definition, or method after a sentence or paragraph boundary

patterns.name: Punctuation and layout boundaries
patterns.context: These markers are adjacent to or co-occur with activated words; some examples occur at formula, quotation, or paragraph boundaries

patterns.name: English function words and phrases
patterns.context: Occurs in explanatory or argumentative sentences and may be jointly triggered by surrounding sentence structure and cohesion

patterns.name: Local Spanish vocabulary
patterns.context: Occurs in Spanish parliamentary speeches, with activations scattered across in-sentence words and no clear English counterpart

patterns.name: Text adjacent to formulas and mathematical notation
patterns.context: Mathematical symbols, formulas, or LaTeX markup are adjacent to body text and sentence boundaries

patterns.name: Forum questions and subjective judgments
patterns.context: A forum question follows a separator, then comments on the question’s subjectivity and related dogma

8_962.description: 激活分布在句界、段落边界及论述推进处，常伴随转折、递进或解释性功能词；也覆盖数学公式邻接文本、西班牙语政治发言和论坛提问，未见单一稳定词项或主题。

patterns.name: 句首转折或递进连接词
patterns.trigger: 句首或句中表示转折、递进的连接词，如 “Since”、“However”、“More recently”、“Further”、“Justo ayer”
patterns.context: 连接前文与后续论述，常位于逗号或句号附近；英文与西班牙文均有例子

patterns.name: 句界后的篇章推进
patterns.trigger: 句号后的 “From now on”、“Taking”、“Let”、“A proof”、“Numerical approaches”等
patterns.context: 句界或段落边界后引出下一步说明、定义或方法

patterns.name: 标点及排版边界
patterns.context: 这些标记紧邻或伴随激活词；部分例子处于公式、引用或段落边界

patterns.name: 英语功能词与短语
patterns.context: 出现在解释或论证句中，可能与前后句式和连接关系共同触发

patterns.name: 西班牙语局部词汇
patterns.context: 出现在西班牙语议会发言中，激活分散在句中词语，缺乏明显的英语对应
patterns.domain: EuroParl 西班牙语政治发言

patterns.name: 公式与数学文本邻接
patterns.context: 数学符号、公式或 LaTeX 标记邻接正文和句界

patterns.name: 论坛提问与主观判断
patterns.context: 由分隔线引出论坛提问，随后评论问题的主观性及相关 dogma

en.description: The most stable trigger is County in geographic proper names, especially when a county name is followed by a comma and state name.
